items.t: Said that under his bill, it would be a misdemeanor to enter or remain in Tennessee after being told to leave the country.
items.q: When someone has exhausted all their options and they’ve been told to leave the country, it is illegal for them to stay, both under federal law, and if this bill passes, it would be a misdemeanor for them to enter in, or remain in, the state of Tennessee,

items.t: Said the Covenant School shooting was "not about this one gun."
items.q: The remarks coincided with others on Lamberth for his take on defending assault weapons , particularly one in which he stated the tragic Covenant School shooting was "not about this one gun.

items.t: Said, with Jeremy Faison, that they would welcome any expelled member who is reappointed and expect them to follow House rules and state law.
items.q: Should any expelled member be reappointed, we will welcome them. Like everyone else, they are expected to follow the rules of the House as well as state law.

record.t: Serves as the Tennessee House Majority Leader.
record.q: Jack Johnson serves as the Tennessee Senate Majority Leader, and William Lamberth serves as the Tennessee House Majority Leader.

record.t: Sponsored a bill on state immigration enforcement.
record.q: Tennessee House Majority Leader William Lamberth, the bill’s sponsor, framed the proposal as a direct challenge to long-standing limits on state immigration enforcement.

record.t: Sponsored a bill that gives public schools the option to check students’ legal residency status and to deny admittance to illegal immigrants.
record.q: House Majority Leader William Lamberth, the bill’s sponsor, expressed concern that Tennessee could lose approximately $1.1 billion in federal funding for education. There is concern that the bill, which gives public schools the option to check students’ legal residency status and the option to deny admittance to illegal immigrants, is in violation of federal law.
